gen-gf-snowburst-one-fs-familjen-grotesk: Cut-stencil swagger, all tall letters and wide bridges, makes Snowburst One a headline-only kind of font, best when big and short. Familjen Grotesk follows in a lively sans whose bowls stay open on one side.
gen-gf-tektur-fs-hind: Hind reads quick and level, its lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals. Tektur bends bendy pipe-cleaner strokes into oversized, expressive letters, while Hind just gets on with being a plain sans.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-fs-nunito: Glowing tube lettering with a splayed c, Tilt Neon holds every stem and tail to one rope-like line. Nunito's big round bowls keep the reading soft.
gen-gf-unkempt-fs-amulya: Amulya reads modern and open, its curves leaving generous gaps as a sans-serif should. And Unkempt, with no hairline anywhere against its thick stems, gives that openness a rough, commanding front.
gen-gf-unkempt-fs-chillax: Relaxed is the first word for Chillax, a sans-serif of spaghetti lines. Unkempt stamps its commanding headings on top, with a sturdy t and a c that never closes into an o, and Chillax loosens everything beneath.
gen-gf-unkempt-fs-plein: Unkempt writes like a steady marker, its t built with crossbar and stem of matching weight, so the headings feel expressive and commanding. Plein handles the quiet, tidy reading.
gen-gf-unkempt-fs-roundo: Roundo reads as a geometric sans, its n built with arch and stem matching and every small counter left unclogged. Unkempt's marker-thick, commanding headings are the loud counterpart.
gen-gf-unkempt-fs-spline-sans: Unkempt brings a commanding, hand-marked voice, with a t whose crossbar and stem match in weight. Spline Sans answers in a contemporary sans, wide gaps between curve ends and stems, so the pair's strongest quality is loud-meets-open.
gen-gf-unkempt-fs-synonym: Synonym lays down a plain stripe of constant ink, with generous openings in every curve, and feels dependable. Synonym then lets Unkempt, expressive and commanding, do the shouting; a big heading size would suit it.
gen-gf-unkempt-outfit: Outfit bends its sans strokes like cable, with no swelling or thinning, and lets each curve stop short of closing. Unkempt is the one that commands, while Outfit simply keeps reading clean.
